column2: The Ziphites come from parched land and present David sheltering on Echela opposite Jessaimoun; Behold and the selected place chain remain.
Saul descends with three thousand chosen Israelites to seek David in Ziph's wilderness, repeated as both destination and search setting.
Saul's roadside camp at Echela contrasts with David's wilderness residence and recognition of pursuit; the repeated wilderness setting remains.
David's spies establish that Saul came prepared from Keilah. Prepared and the selected origin are not replaced by an idiom of certainty.
David secretly enters the sleeping place, with Abner's name and rank, Saul's covered carriage and surrounding camp all retained.
column3: Covered carriage for lampene is provisional; the narrative is not silently changed to a trench or wagon-circle.

column2: Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, receive the invitation; Abishai volunteers. Ahimelech is distinct from Abimelech the priest in previous chapters.
The nighttime entry reveals Saul lying asleep, spear in the ground at his head and Abner's people around him. There was carries idou; lying asleep avoids an unsupported intensity adverb.
Abishai attributes the enemy's enclosure to the Lord and proposes one spear strike into the ground without a second. The claim and proposal remain his speech.
Propose For before the question grounding David's prohibition. Humble follows tapeinoo, and the question concerns striking the Lord's anointed and being acquitted.
column3: Humble is a provisional contextual rendering in a proposed killing scene; it is not reduced to emotional embarrassment or replaced without noting the source verb.

column2: The oath assures divine striking or death on his day or descent into war and being added; the alternatives and selected added verb remain.
column3: Ean me is construed as oath assurance; added leaves the implied destination unstated rather than inserting a specific death formula.

column2: The same negative-oath formula as 24:7 precedes the instruction to take spear and water flask and depart by themselves; human and divine titles remain distinct.
David takes both items and the pair leaves; no one sees, knows or wakes because all sleep under the Lord's stupor. The three negatives and divine cause remain.
column3: Stupor for thambos describes this sleep context without a clinical claim.

column2: David crosses to the far side and stands at a distant summit with a long intervening way; the repeated distance markers remain.
David calls the people and specifically Abner, who answers by asking the caller's identity; the two speakers remain explicit.
Propose For before the explanation that a person entered to destroy the king. Questions about Abner's manhood, uniqueness and failed guarding remain.

David calls the act not good, swears the plural guards are sons of execution and points to the missing spear and water flask at the head. The plural audience is retained through sons and you who guard.
Saul recognizes child David's voice; David answers Your servant, lord king. The elliptical self-identification and human honorific remain.
Propose For before the questions about sin and wrong as grounds for challenging pursuit. My lord and his servant remain the respectful third-person frame within direct speech.
The king must hear: if God instigates, may He smell the king's sacrifice; if humans do, they are cursed for expulsion from the inheritance and the command to serve other gods.
column3: God is discussed in third person, so He is appropriate rather than Thou; the sacrificial smell and expulsion image are not abstracted away.

column2: Propose For before the explanation that Israel's king seeks David's soul. The wish against spilled blood opposite the Lord's presence and the night-raven's mountain pursuit remain.
column3: The selected bird is not changed to a partridge, and the unusual pursuit comparison is not silently reconstructed.

column2: Saul confesses, invites return, promises no harm because his soul was honored, then admits vain action and great ignorance; the explicit causal link remains.
Here is presents the king's spear and calls for one young man to retrieve it; the singular retrieval is not expanded to return of the unmentioned flask.

The Lord's future repayment of each person's righteous deeds and faithfulness is grounded in delivery and David's refusal to strike the anointed. Plural righteous deeds remains distinct from an abstract status alone.
Behold introduces the comparison of magnified souls, with today's doubled timing, wishes for magnification and shelter, then future rescue from every affliction.
column3: The shift from optative wish to future rescue is preserved rather than making every verb a wish.

column2: Saul blesses child David and emphatically predicts doing and ability; their separate departures follow. Both cognate emphases are expressed by surely.
David's inner speech predicts being added into Saul's hands, sees no good except escape and cessation of search, and anticipates rescue from his hand.
column3: Added is retained as a difficult threat expression; the confidence is David's deliberation rather than a new divine oracle.

column2: David and four hundred men go to Achish son of Ammach at Gath; the selected troop number and patronymic are preserved.
Each man stays with his household, and David with both Ahinoam and Abigail, still identified as Nabal's wife. The two wives' names and provenance remain.
The report of flight to Gath leads Saul to cease seeking David; no additional treaty is inferred.
David requests a country town if favored and questions residence in a royal city. The unnamed plural let them give remains rather than silently changing the request's grammatical subject.
Achish's implicit giving of Ziklag explains its belonging to the singular king of Judea to this day; the selected singular royal recipient remains.
David's stay is four months; no added year is imported or used to harmonize a later duration.
David and his men attack all the Gesiri and Amalekite, followed by Behold and the inhabited fortified land from Gelampsour to Egypt.
column3: Suitable fortified settlements is the inherited provisional rendering of a difficult compressed habitation phrase; the inhabitants and geographic syntax need fuller review.

column2: David strikes and leaves neither man nor woman alive, taking five named kinds of property; the return then shifts to plural they. The killings and change of grammatical number remain.
Propose you all in Achish's question to preserve the plural verb addressed to David as the party's representative. David's reported southern targets retain Judea, Jesmega and Kenezi.
No survivors are brought to Gath lest they report David's practice; that practice continues throughout his foreign stay. The narrative's stated concealment motive remains explicit.
David is greatly trusted by Achish, whose quoted conclusion predicts perpetual slavery. The inherited passive and clarified speaker preserve the compressed Greek agency.
column3: Has made himself utterly shamed interprets the perfect middle/passive shame construction reflexively; has been utterly shamed is also possible. Achish's inference is not narrator confirmation of Israel's attitude.
